channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Iran live updates: US military repositions personnel at Mideast bases, source says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Teen's alleged rape at frat near Univ. of Chicago follows prior incidents: Lawsuit
item.description: An unnamed teenager has filed a lawsuit against a fraternity alleging it did not do enough to prevent sexual assaults, despite incidents dating back to 2009.

item.title: UK seeks tougher laws to deter undersea pipeline attacks
item.description: An inadequate law from the 19th century must be strengthened to deter saboteurs from attacking the UK's critical undersea cables and pipelines, a minister has said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial: Judge denies request to question holdout juror
item.description: The Massachusetts mother's murder trial ended in a mistrial last month.

item.title: WATCH: American farms honor Dolly Parton with themed corn maze
item.description: Nearly two dozen farms across the country are featuring a Dolly Parton themed corn maze this fall. ABC News' Reena Roy takes us along as she finds her way through one of them in New Jersey.

item.title: Sudan’s war escalates as UN warns of wider regional crisis
item.description: In tonight’s edition: Sudan’s brutal war continues to take a devastating regional toll, as a drone strike in Abyei reportedly kills 153 people. We speak to the UN envoy for Sudan following an emergency international meeting on the escalating crisis. Also, health authorities prepare to coordinate a response as Ebola cases emerge in Nigeria and rise in Kenya. Finally, ten years after Cameroon’s deadliest railway disaster, families of the 79 victims are still fighting for justice, saying their pain has yet to be acknowledged.

item.title: Florida mayor arrested on grand theft and fraud charges over COVID relief funds: AG
item.description: Kissimmee Mayor Jackie Espinosa is being charged with grand theft and organized scheme to defraud, according to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier.

item.title: Trump admin 'destroying' US democracy with 'autocratic, terrorist version of Christian nationalism'
item.description: François Picard welcomes former US Assistant Secretary of Defense Jim Townsend and former US Air Force officer Michael (Mikey) Weinstein, founder and president of the Military Religious Freedom Foundation. Is American military power becoming an instrument of political and religious coercion, both at home and abroad? From the reported restrictions on Ukraine's access to Starlink satellite communications to the Trump administration's overtures towards Vladimir Putin and the growing controversy over religious ideology within the Pentagon, the two guests offer a stark assessment of the direction of American foreign and defence policy.

item.title: Vance praises Ramaswamy for having 'audacity' to run controversial Acton ad
item.description: Vance defended Ramaswamy's ad showing Acton's estranged mother.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV needs no further lung cancer treatment, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, 71, will require no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localised, the Vatican said Wednesday. The pontiff underwent surgery last week to remove part of his right lung after being diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. He was discharged Saturday and will gradually resume activities.

item.title: WATCH: WNBA finals head to Atlanta for Game 3
item.description: The Atlanta Dream look to take the series lead after their Game 2 win. ESPN senior writer Michael Voepel previews Game 3 at State Farm Arena.

item.title: Airbnb's new rules limit cleaning chores for guests
item.description: Under the new policy, hosts can no longer require guests to strip beds or wash and put away dishes.

item.title: In run-up to mass protests and riots, pro-Russian accounts amplified French anger, NGO finds
item.description: Research carried out by the Alliance4Europe NGO suggests that pro-Russian networks manipulated information online in an effort to exacerbate anger in France ahead of last weekend's massive protests and subsequent unrest. After analysing more than half a million posts across various social media platforms, the group says it was able to track the campaign back to the start of September. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Omri Preiss, Managing Director at the Alliance4Europe.

item.title: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal
item.description: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. Meta called the penalty “a tax on speech.”

item.title: French bond yields hit 24-year high after unrest
item.description: French bond yields have topped 5%, their highest level since 2002, after widespread protests and violence over the weekend. It's a sign that investors are losing confidence in France's finances, as the government grapples with budget and debt problems. Also in the show - chipmaker Nvidia says it's invested $10 billion in European tech firms to boost the 'AI economy,' and the UK approves a controversial natural gas field as PM Andy Burnham faces pressure over energy costs.

item.title: EU prosecutors search European Parliament offices of far-right group
item.description: The far-right European Parliament group of French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen's party said Wednesday EU prosecutors were searching its offices as part of a graft probe into its now-defunct predecessor. The Patriots for Europe group said the European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) had been searching its administrative offices in Brussels and Strasbourg "since this morning". FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Strasbourg.

item.title: Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling
item.description: The top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are working under the presumption that the president will seek to justify election interference by alleging fraud.

item.title: Pope Leo's doctors say tests show he needs no further treatment for lung cancer
item.description: Pope Leo's doctors say final tissue and molecular tests have confirmed his lung cancer was localised, and no further treatment is needed, the Vatican said in a statement.

item.title: Putin agrees to resume three-way talks with Kyiv and Washington
item.description: President ⁠Volodymyr Zelenskiy ​said on Wednesday ​that Ukraine supported a US proposal for ​three-way talks ‌with Russia ⁠and the United ‌States at the level ⁠of negotiators to be held as soon ​as possible, preferably ‌no later than early November. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia Programme at Chatham House, says that "it's not clear whether Putin would meet Trump and Zelensky", adding that "meeting Zelensky is the last thing that Putin would be prepared to do".

item.title: Trump exploits France riots to push false immigration claims ahead of midterms
item.description: Donald Trump and his inner circle are using unrest in France to push unsubstantiated claims blaming the riots on immigration, even showing French protest footage at midterm rallies. But there is no evidence linking immigration to the unrest, and it's prompted French President Emmanuel Macron to accuse world leaders of making “stupid comments” at France’s expense. Trump’s focus comes as Republicans face mounting pressure ahead of the midterms and his approval rating hits a reported record low.

item.title: 'Neither the Sudanese military, nor the RSF take any acknowledgement of human life in this war'
item.description: The death toll from a drone strike Monday on a market in an area disputed between Sudan and South Sudan has risen to 153 and is likely even higher, a local official told AFP on Wednesday. Authorities in Abyei district said the strike on the Amiet market involved the use of multiple munitions and was carried out by the Sudanese army. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Jan Pospisil, Sudan Affairs Analyst at the Peace and Conflict Resolution Evidence Platform. He says that for a long time the Sudanese army has tried "to portray a picture internationally that they are humane, whereas RSF is committing atrocities. Here we see very clearly that there is not much difference between these two".

item.title: Football regulator to address EFL clubs as quest for deal goes on
item.description: The head of English football's watchdog will address the 72 clubs below the top flight on Thursday as the quest for a financial redistribution deal with the Premier League continues.

item.title: Le Pen sees polls boost amid mass protests, riots
item.description: Marine Le Pen is set to officially launch her presidential campaign this weekend at the National Rally two-day party congress in Orléans. The latest Ifop poll, carried out in the wake of the mass protests and riots in France, suggests the far right leader would win the first round of the presidential election by a wide margin, and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerged as her most likely opponent in the runoff. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Trump faces fresh questions over ties to 'humanitarian' Putin
item.description: US President Donald Trump's pivot away from Ukraine has triggered fresh questions about his attachment to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, the man a top American envoy flattered on Wednesday as a "humanitarian. Trump has cast his dealings with Putin as part of a mega-deal that has secured the release of American detainee Stephen Hubbard -- and which Trump says will end Russia's war on Ukraine. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kharkiv.

item.title: Canadian publisher drops author Orelien after confirming he used AI in debut novel
item.description: The Canadian publisher representing Thélyson Orélien on Wednesday said it had dropped the prize-nominated writer over new information indicating that he did use artificial intelligence to write his acclaimed debut.

item.title: Police given more time to question two men re-arrested in RAF Fairford investigation
item.description: Two men who were re-arrested as part of an investigation into a suspected terror plot near RAF Fairford can be held for up to seven days after police were given more time to question them.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals 'Best of the World' destinations
item.description: National Geographic editor-in-chief Nathan Lump talks about must-visit destinations for 2027.

item.title: Macron visits Riyadh to show solidarity amid Houthi attacks, ease tensions at home via fuel deal
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday paid an unannounced visit to Riyadh in a bid to underscore French support for the kingdom amid intensified attacks by Houthi rebels and an attempt to ease tensions at home by securing oil and diesel imports.

item.title: Cowardly killers who refuse to attend sentencing will face new penalties
item.description: Killers who refuse to attend sentence hearings could be confined to their cell for weeks or lose visiting privileges.

item.title: Greece: Protesters draw inspiration from demonstrations in France
item.description: Inspired by protests in France and other parts of Europe, thousands of Greek students on Wednesday demonstrated around the country.

item.title: World set to breach 1.5°C warming limit set by Paris Climate Agreement
item.description: The UN is warning that global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals of 1.5 degrees Celsius warming – and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century. The report by the United Nations Environment Programme lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November's COP31 climate summit - set to take place next month in Turkey. Story by Emerald Maxwell.

item.title: French President Macron lands in Saudi Arabia on surprise 'solidarity' visit
item.description: ⁠French President Emmanuel ​Macron landed in Riyadh on Wednseday, ‌adding an ⁠unscheduled stop to his ‌ongoing tour of the Gulf ⁠region. The president's office said the visit aimed to demonstrate “France's solidarity” ​with Saudi Arabia in ‌the face of attacks launched by the ‌Houthis against its territory. Details by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Douglas Herbert.

item.title: Kremlin says 'ready' to resume 3-way talks with US and Ukraine mid-November
item.description: Moscow is ready to resume trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks next month, the Kremlin said Wednesday after President Vladimir Putin met with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Russia. FRANCE 24's correspondent Gulliver Cragg has more.

item.title: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump admin restrictions on medical care for trans inmates
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected a Trump administration appeal seeking to immediately enforce medical care restrictions for transgender people in prison

item.title: Macron rejects Trump’s claims blaming migrants for French riots
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron condemned comments by "foreign leaders" on the violent protests in France on October 17. He has now arrived in Saudi Arabia as part of his Gulf tour.

item.title: France: Far right leader Marine Le Pen gains popularity amid nationwide riots
item.description: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu met with union leaders today in France. His government admitted law enforcement officers had lost control this past weekend during protests which resulted in scenes of violence and looting. The country is bracing for more protests – the Yellow Vest movement called on demonstrators to take to the street on Saturday. As the events unfold, far-right leader Marine Le Pen is gaining popularity. Details and analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi.

item.title: Some Brazilians long associated with the left now shift towards Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description: In the first round of Brazil’s presidential elections, Flavio Bolsonaro got the most votes in 15 electoral districts in the North Zone of Rio de Janeiro, compared with 9 for Lula. This part of the city, long associated with the left and the social policies of Lula’s Workers’ Party, is now shifting towards former president Jair Bolsonaro’s son.

item.title: 70% of water produced in Guadeloupe never reaches homes
item.description: In the French overseas territory of Guadeloupe, a water crisis is a daily reality, with some residents going without water for weeks. The network is being repaired, but at the current pace, France's Court of Auditors says replacing all of it would take 208 years. Now, a judicial investigation has been opened in Paris into the crisis, following a citizen-led legal action. Our France 2 colleagues report.

item.title: Sentenced to death at 17, at 68, quilt artist receives solo museum exhibition
item.description: A quilt artist who spent decades on death row now has his first solo exhibit at the Grand Rapids Art Museum.

item.title: Italy: Giorgia Meloni approves tougher anti-riot laws after Milan violence 🇮🇹
item.description: Italy approved a raft of security measures on Tuesday including a new offence of violent participation in a demonstration, tougher penalties for rioters, and financial liability for parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.

item.title: Amy Acton campaign slams Ramaswamy over controversial ad featuring estranged mother
item.description: Ohio Gubernatorial Candidate Amy Acton’s campaign alleged her opponent's campaign is using her estranged mother in a controversial political ad against her.

item.title: WATCH: Controversy brews over home of Winnie the Pooh
item.description: ABC News' Danny New examines a controversy about where the stuffed bear that inspired Winnie the Pooh should reside: in England or the New York Public Library?

item.description: Surveillance video shows 27-year-old Ebro Ahmed jumping onto a bus to stop it after he noticed the driver having a medical emergency.

item.description: The pontiff made his way through St. Peter's Square in the Popemobile one week after undergoing lung cancer surgery.

item.title: Israel frees dozens of Americans, including U.S. Congress nominee, after West Bank detention
item.description: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander along with dozens of American and Israeli rabbis and activists were helping Palestinian olive harvesters when they were detained by Israeli forces.

item.description: Government and business websites around the world were taken down in a bid to protect organisations after a critical software update was issued over vulnerabilities in programming language.

item.title: Vital clues could help predict prostate cancer years in advance
item.description: Scientists have found clues that could help predict who will develop aggressive prostate cancer many years in advance.

item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has criticized foreign leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump, saying they exploit unrest in France for political gain

item.title: Trump leans into unprecedented power ahead of midterm elections
item.description: Less than two weeks before Election Day, President Trump continues to crash through barriers that he wouldn't dare cross in his first term.

item.description: A critical incident at a NHS Trust has ended after the number of people waiting for assessment in A&E "dropped significantly" - but hospital bosses warned patients still face "long waits".

item.description: Police are investigating former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson over an allegation that he raped a woman in the Houses of Parliament, the PA news agency reports.

item.description: Nearly $1 million in rare trading cards were stolen from a FedEx truck parked near a Southern California business that authenticates and grades the collectible items, according to police.

item.description: A Garda investigation has been launched after two bodies were discovered in Ireland.

item.description: Three quarters of perpetrators who carried out workplace attacks exhibited behaviors of concern: US Secret Service

item.description: A drone strike on a fuel depot in a disputed region on the Sudan-South Sudan border has killed at least 153 people.

item.title: Childcare costs weigh on some voters before the midterm elections
item.description: Rising childcare costs are a factor for parents weighing how to vote in November's midterm elections

item.title: Man arrested in Pakistan over $126m counterfeit postage scheme
item.description: A man has been arrested in Pakistan and accused of running a counterfeit postage operation costing the US Postal Service $126m (£94m).

item.title: Uganda reacts angrily as Nigeria confirms its first Ebola case
item.description: Nigeria has recorded its first case of Ebola during the current outbreak, the country's health ministry has said - as the virus continues to spread internationally.

item.title: WATCH: Great white shark leaps out of ocean off California's Marina Beach
item.description: A great white shark surprised visitors off Marina Beach, California, when it leapt out of the ocean as a beachgoer was taking a video.

item.description: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bill Taylor reacts to the latest comments from President Donald Trump on Russia as questions grow over America's support of Ukraine.

item.description: A New Jersey food importer filed a lawsuit Tuesday challenging President Donald Trump’s power to invoke a Depression-era law to levy a 50% tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods

item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed in a shark attack at a popular beach on South Africa's southeastern coast, local authorities said.

item.title: WATCH: Wirecutter shares top picks after 15 years of product testing
item.description: Jason Chen of The New York Times' Wirecutter shares the technological products that are most loved by readers.

item.description: ABC News' Ian Pannell reports on the state of the agency, which says it's been providing food to around 1.6 million people every month since last year's ceasefire announcement.
